newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS to follow BA fare price increase.
newsitem.headline: SAS to follow BA fare price increase.

text.p: Scandianvian Airlines System (SAS) will raise fares by 2.5 percent on its Scandinavia-UK routes following a move by British Airways which was sparked by higher jet fuel prices, an SAS spokesman said on Wednesday.

British Airways Plc said it was increasing full published fares on its European routes by an average 2.5 percent from mid-October because of the soaring cost of jet fuel, which has risen by 30 percent since mid-July.

"We will follow with an increase of 2.5 percent on all official IATA fares...for SAS it's only concerning UK-Scandinavia, and it's only fares sold in the UK," said Ulf Ingnas, a spokesman for SAS Western European routes.
"We are also buying fuel in the UK for all of our operations into the UK, so we are just as much affected by this as British Airways is on our UK-Scandinavia routes," he told Reuters.
BA said it was considering increases on long-haul routes.
Ingnas said for the time being SAS planned to absorb increased fuel costs on other routes instead of passing them on to customers, but said this could change.
"There is no intention at the moment for further steps. (But) I can't say this is something that will last forever."
SAS is partially owned by the governments of Sweden, Denmark and Norway.

Jet fuel on the European spot market has risen by 30 percent since mid-July as world oil prices rocketed on a bullish cocktail of Middle East tension, low stocks and strong demand in the approach to winter.
